MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Diagnosis: Lung adenocarcinoma favored
Specimen Type: FFPE tissue from pelvic bone biopsy
Estimated Tumor Content: 40%

TEST PERFORMED
Comprehensive Molecular Profiling Assay
- DNA Panel: 45 genes
- RNA Panel: 17 fusion kinase genes (attempted)

METHODOLOGY
This assay utilizes barcoded primer technology with an integrated sequencer platform for simultaneous detection of mutations, insertions/deletions, and gene rearrangements. DNA sequencing has a detection threshold of ≥5% variant allele frequency with minimum 100x coverage. RNA analysis targets fusion transcripts in 17 kinase genes.

RESULTS SUMMARY

DNA PANEL - COMPLETED
Key Actionable Genes Tested:
• EGFR (NM_005228.5): No variants detected
• KRAS (NM_033360.4): No variants detected  
• BRAF (NM_004333.6): No variants detected

Additional genes analyzed (complete list available upon request): No clinically significant variants detected in the examined regions of the 45-gene panel.

RNA PANEL - FAILED
Targeted Fusion/Rearrangement Genes:
• ALK
• ROS1
• RET
• MET
• NTRK1/2/3
• Additional kinase genes (12 total)

Result: Analysis could not be completed due to insufficient RNA quality

QUALITY INDICATORS
DNA Quality: Adequate
DNA Quantity: Sufficient
Mean Coverage Depth: 342x
RNA Quality: Poor (RIN <2.0)
RNA Quantity: Insufficient for analysis

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
The absence of detectable variants in EGFR, KRAS, and BRAF suggests this tumor is unlikely to respond to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., erlotinib, gefitinib, osimertinib), MEK inhibitors, or BRAF inhibitors.

The RNA panel failure prevents assessment of ALK, ROS1, RET, MET, and NTRK gene rearrangements. Therefore, potential benefit from ALK inhibitors (e.g., alectinib, crizotinib), ROS1 inhibitors (e.g., entrectinib, crizotinib), RET inhibitors (e.g., selpercatinib), MET inhibitors, or NTRK inhibitors cannot be determined from this specimen.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Given the RNA panel failure, consider repeat testing using material from a separate specimen if clinically indicated, particularly to assess for targetable gene fusions that occur in 10-15% of lung adenocarcinomas.

ASSAY LIMITATIONS
• This assay detects variants present at ≥5% allele frequency
• Not all exons/introns of all genes are sequenced
• Complex structural variants may not be detected
• RNA quality issues may prevent fusion detection
• Results should be interpreted in context of all clinical and pathological findings

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
